attempts.summary: Implemented, via an Ansible playbook run from control_node node5, a VRRP-backed single gateway address on node3's LAN for reaching node4 across the node1/node2 VyOS router pair. node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100) each got eth1 (lan-a, node3's network) and eth2 (lan-b, node4's network) addressed, with VRRP group LAN-A (vrid 10, VIP 10.10.1.1/24) on eth1 and LAN-B (vrid 20, VIP 10.10.2.1/24) on eth2, preempt enabled by default so node1 reclaims master whenever healthy. node3 was given static IP 10.10.1.12/24 plus a dedicated route to node4's subnet (10.10.2.0/24) via the single gateway 10.10.1.1, without disturbing its existing mgmt/internet default route. node4 symmetrically got 10.10.2.13/24 plus a route to node3's subnet via 10.10.2.1, so return traffic works regardless of which router is active. Failover was demonstrated live: disabling node1's eth1+eth2 promoted node2 to MASTER on both VRRP groups within seconds while node3->node4 connectivity was preserved throughout; re-enabling node1 caused it to preempt back to MASTER on both groups (200 > 100) with node2 returning cleanly to BACKUP. All 5 managed nodes (node1, node2, node3, node4, node5) were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms; each was confirmed to have a new boot_id post-restart, and required state (VyOS interface/VRRP config, VRRP MASTER/BACKUP roles, CentOS static IP/route config, node3->node4 reachability) was independently re-verified after every restart before proceeding to the next node.
